history.summary: A 926 sqft compact 3BR at The Lakeshore (2007, 848 units, 77yr lease left) asking $1.36M / $1,469 psf, 160-190m from Lakeside MRT (EW26) in D22/OCR. The asset is sound and liquid, but the price carries no edge: the exact same 926 sqft type transacted at $1,360,000 / $1,469 psf in Oct-2025, and the cohort's last-12mo median is $1,464 psf. Worse, this compact sub-cohort is the project's laggard — flat since 2024 ($1,499 -> $1,486 -> $1,459 median psf) while the 1,109-1,227 sqft 3BRs ran from $1,443 to $1,533 psf.
history.rating_rationale: Priced exactly at its own cohort's market, in the cohort that has stopped moving. Verified against 154 URA prints for the project (64 in the last 24mo): the 900-1,000 sqft band's 24mo median is $1,486 psf and its last-12mo median $1,464 psf vs this $1,469 psf ask — a dead-on-market price, not a discount. An identical 926 sqft unit printed at $1,360,000 / $1,469 psf in Oct-2025, so the ask is literally last October's price. `relative_value` agrees: +3.0% vs the age-adjusted D22 median for its 800-1,050 size band. The single robust forward signal in the backtest — cheap-vs-peers — is therefore neutral-to-negative here, and a Buy needs it. The algo's score_1000 = 812 is built mostly on channels the priors de-weight or invert: appreciation +7.39 is the trailing 5yr URA CAGR (6.46%), which has ~0 forward power and whose own momentum field reads -1.0; yield +11.95 is the largest single component and high gross yield predicts LOWER forward price growth (std_beta -0.16), so it is carry, not appreciation. That yield is also overstated for THIS unit: the $5,300 rent is a project x 3BR average dominated by the 1,109-1,227 sqft pool (97 of 154 prints), while the live 926 sqft rental ask at The Lakeshore is $4,800 — re-scoring at $4,800 drops score_1000 to ~794 and gross yield to 4.24%. What is genuinely real and forward-relevant: OCR region (+3.7%/yr baseline, the strongest), exceptional transit (160-190m to Lakeside EW26), deep exit liquidity (848 units, 1,628 lifetime transactions, 64 prints in 24mo, a $1.36M quantum in the deepest buyer band), and 77 years of lease with no decay cliff inside a 5-7yr hold. That combination makes this a safe, easy-to-exit hold — it does not make it an outperformer bought at market. Against it: 2027-28 completions land inside the hold window — The LakeGarden Residences (306 units, TOP Aug-2027) and Sora, both on Yuan Ching Rd minutes away — competing for the same Lakeside tenant and resale story; and the JLD build-out is a narrative with no measured forward power plus proven execution risk (the 2024 master-developer tender drew no award; the 1,200-unit Town Hall Link White Site only reached the Confirmed List in Jul-2026, tender closing 17-Nov-2026). Neutral: a fine asset at a fair price is a hold-quality Neutral, not a Buy. It would become interesting nearer $1.28-1.30M (~$1,390 psf), which the cohort has printed as recently as Nov-2025.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Solid but overstated in the dossier. Live Lakeshore 3BR asks: 926 sqft $4,800/mo, 1,109 sqft $5,400-5,500, 1,173 sqft $5,800. The $5,300 in factual_data is a project x 3BR average pulled up by the large-unit pool, so treat ~$4,600-4,800 achieved as the working number -> ~4.1-4.2% gross, ~2.5% net. Tenant demand is real (NTU/NUS staff, Jurong industrial and IBP employment, 2-min MRT walk), but a 926 sqft 3BR is the weak product in its own project: the 1,109 sqft unit costs a tenant only ~$600/mo more, and 2027-28 completions at LakeGarden and Sora will add newer stock to the same catchment.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The headline 6.46% 5yr CAGR is real at project level and NOT a size-mix artifact — decomposed by band, 2BR ran ~6.1%/yr, the compact 3BR ~6.5%/yr and the large 3BR ~9.4%/yr from 21/22 to 25/26. But nearly all of it was booked by 2024, and the subject's own band has since stalled: median psf 1,499 (2024) -> 1,486 (2025) -> 1,459 (2026), last-12mo $1,464 vs prior-12mo $1,491, even as the 1,100-1,250 band kept climbing to $1,533. Forward, the trailing number carries ~0 predictive weight; what remains is the OCR baseline (+3.7%/yr) minus a cohort that is not participating and 2027-28 supply arriving in the window. I carry ~3.8%/yr, below the dossier's 6.46%, which cuts the modelled 5yr annualized ROI from ~6.9% toward ~5%.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Unresearched — no profile exists for The Lakeshore and the listing record carries no floor, facing or stack, so no stack join was possible. What the prints do show: 926 sqft is a genuine Lakeshore type (27 all-time prints in the 900-1,000 band, sizes 926/936/947), so this is NOT a mis-scraped sqft or bedroom-count artifact. Floor is not a large swing factor in this cohort — recent prints run $1,404-1,531 psf across floors 6-10, 11-15 and 16-20 with no clean gradient. Unverified and worth checking before any offer: which block/outlook (Jurong Lake / pool vs Jurong West HDB and the Boon Lay Way traffic side).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale URA evidence, not portal headline: 154 project prints decomposed by size band. Subject's 900-1,000 sqft band median psf 1,499 (2024) -> 1,486 (2025) -> 1,459 (2026); last-12mo $1,464 vs prior-12mo $1,491 = flat-to-down, while the project's 1,100-1,250 band rose $1,443 -> $1,533. Forward rate set to roughly the OCR realized baseline (+3.7%/yr), with the MRT/JLD positives offset by the cohort plateau and by 2027-28 competing completions (LakeGarden TOP Aug-2027, Sora). Replaces the 6.46% trailing 5yr CAGR, which is backward-loaded to the 2021-24 run-up and carries ~0 forward power.
